description: Save one native split as one durable Pin and validate both panes, layout, profile ownership, and teardown.
preconditions: Launch the exact completed Dev build with the isolated split-pins profile
Use one active Space and keep an unrelated ordinary tab open
steps: Open two different HTTP or HTTPS pages and create a native split; focus the second pane and drag the divider away from center
Use the split tab context menu to choose Pin split view; inspect the sidebar and interact with both pages
Close the Pin from its sidebar row, then reopen it twice
Change the split to stacked, reverse the panes, focus the second pane, quit normally, and relaunch the same isolated profile
Navigate each pane away from its saved home, then choose Reset to home from the Pin menu
Close only one pane, then activate its saved Pin; repeat with the other pane
Repeat saving with the same URL open in both panes
Unpin the pair by dragging the durable row into ordinary tabs, then Pin and remove it through its menu
Create a split starting from an existing Pin, then close and reopen the resulting Pin
Stop the isolated profile after checking persistence
observables: Saving replaces the native split row with exactly one Pin row that names both pages; tab count and each live page state remain unchanged
Saved splits have a split glyph and an accessible Split view description. Their row menu offers Reset to home when live, disables it when closed, and omits Favorite.
Reopening restores exactly two panes with their saved home URLs, order, layout, ratio, and focus; repeated activation adds no tabs
Normal quit and relaunch preserves both pane identities even when both URLs are identical
Return Home restores both saved URLs in the existing panes
Closing one pane retains the survivor; activating the Pin creates only its missing counterpart
Unpin and Remove preserve both WebContents as one ordinary native split, clear both persistent associations, and leave no ghost Pin rows
Splitting an existing Pin saves the complete pair without another Pin row
The split stays in its owning Space and profile; other Spaces do not acquire its live instance
Closing and stopping produce no new crash report
